anomaly_def.Name: Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Storage Space Capacity Anomaly + Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly : Costing metadata (row counts, histograms, correlation statistics) no longer matches the real data distribution, leading the optimizer to pick systematically sub-optimal execution plans. 
Storage Space Capacity Anomaly : Free space in data, log, or temporary areas is exhausted or hits hard limits, causing allocation failures and blocking further writes, extensions, or archival activity. 
Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly : Server-side listener, socket, or network bandwidth resources become saturated or unstable, producing connection errors, long handshake times, and slow result-set transfers.

When these three root causes strike concurrently, the database exhibits severe and seemingly unrelated symptoms: queries are mis-planned into scan-heavy or spill-to-disk strategies that inflate temporary-space consumption just as temp, data, or log files approach full capacity; space shortages trigger statement failures, transaction rollbacks, and forced disconnects that in turn cause application retry storms, swelling the number of incoming connections and overwhelming listener queues; overloaded network paths and socket backlogs lengthen fetch times, so mis-estimated queries hold server processes and temp segments for longer, further delaying space reclamation, while log archival blocked by network congestion accelerates log-area exhaustion. Administrators may observe a mixture of extreme cardinality errors in execution plans, rapidly declining or completely exhausted tablespace and log free space, connection-establishment timeouts, rising client-read/write waits, and a surge of "out of space" or "too many connections" errors appearing together in logs.

Causally, stale or missing statistics drive inefficient plans that amplify I/O and temporary-space usage, hastening storage depletion. Imminent space exhaustion can prevent auto-statistics collection or cause DML to fail mid-transaction, keeping statistics perpetually stale and reinforcing bad plans. Space pressure and plan inefficiency prolong execution times, increasing the window during which sessions hold network sockets open; slower data transfer over a congested or capacity-limited network extends this further, piling up active and retrying connections that saturate listener and OS socket resources. Network saturation can also impede remote backups or archive-log shipping, filling log destinations and intensifying the storage crisis. The intertwined feedback loops among poor statistics, space exhaustion, and network contention therefore magnify each individual anomaly, rapidly degrading overall database performance and availability.

entry.official_definition: Terminates any session that has been idle within an open transaction for longer than the specified amount of time.
entry.trigger_condition: A session is idle, waiting for a client query, while an open transaction remains active longer than the configured threshold.
entry.workload_impact: The session is terminated; this prevents long idle transactions from holding locks or preventing vacuum cleanup.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when a statement cannot obtain the required lock within the configured waiting window because another transaction or metadata operation is holding an incompatible lock.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect blocking sessions, reduce conflicting transaction overlap, shorten transaction lifetime, and review lock scheduling and schema-change timing.
